H1.text: Pull a suitcase by its handle. Tow a toy car on a string. Push a lawn mower by its long handle.

H2.text: In all three, you pull at a slant, but the thing moves along the ground.

H3.text: Aarav drags his suitcase to the bus stop. He pulls with forty newtons, along a slanted handle.

H4.text: How much of his forty newtons really moves it forward? All forty, or less?

H5.text: By the end, you will answer it with one small tool, the dot product.

P1.text: So what is the dot product?

P2.text: Shine a torch straight down on a slanted stick. Its shadow on the floor is shorter than the stick.

P3.text: That shadow is the part of the stick that points along the floor.

P4.text: Now take two arrows, A and B. Find the shadow of A on B, and multiply it by the length of B.

P5.text: That is the dot product. The answer is just a number, so it is also called the scalar product.

S1.text: Let's run it on Aarav's suitcase. He pulls with a force F of forty newtons.

S2.text: First, the handle is flat, so theta is zero. The shadow of F on the floor is all forty newtons.

S3.text: Now he raises the handle to sixty degrees. The shadow shrinks to just twenty newtons.

S4.text: The rest of his pull only lifts the handle. It does not roll the suitcase forward.

S5.text: At ninety degrees, he pulls straight up. The shadow is zero. The suitcase does not roll.

S7.text: F points along the handle. Its shadow on the floor is F cos theta. The suitcase moves along d.

S8.text: On the graph, as theta grows, the forward part falls. It follows cos theta.

D1.text: Now the formula, one small step at a time.

D2.text: Step one. Theta is the angle between A and B, measured tail to tail.

D3.text: Step two. The shadow of A on B is A cos theta. Cos theta is the fraction the shadow keeps. One at zero degrees, a half at sixty, zero at ninety.

D4.text: Step three. Multiply by the length of B. A dot B equals A B cos theta.

D5.text: Step four. The shadow of B on A, times A, gives the same number. So A dot B equals B dot A.

T1.text: Remember this. A dot B is one arrow times the shadow of the other. A number, not an arrow.

C1.text: Now, side by side. The angle decides the sign.

C2.text: At sixty degrees, the shadow of A falls forward, along B. The dot product is positive.

C3.text: At one hundred and twenty degrees, the shadow falls backward. The dot product is negative.

C4.text: Now you try. Theta is exactly ninety degrees. Is the dot product positive, negative, or zero? Pause and decide.

C5.text: Zero! At ninety degrees, the shadow shrinks to a single point. And cos ninety is zero.

R1.text: Now, a shortcut exams love. Follow the links.

R2.text: One. i hat and i hat point the same way. Theta is zero, so i dot i is one.

R3.text: Two. i hat and j hat are at ninety degrees, so i dot j is zero. Same for j and k, and k and i.

R4.text: Three. Write A and B in i, j and k, and multiply out. Every mixed pair gives zero.

R5.text: Four. Only matching pairs survive. A dot B equals A x B x, plus A y B y, plus A z B z.

K1.text: Your turn. A is three i plus four j. B is four i minus three j. Are they at right angles? Pause and think.

K2.text: Yes! Twelve minus twelve is zero. A zero dot product means ninety degrees.

W2.text: A is two i, plus two j, plus k. B is three i, plus four k. Find A dot B, and the angle between them.

W3.text: Multiply matching parts. Six, plus zero, plus four. That is ten.

W4.text: Now the sizes. A is the root of four plus four plus one, so three. B is the root of nine plus sixteen, so five.

W5.text: Cos theta equals A dot B, over A times B. Ten over fifteen, which is two thirds.

W6.text: So theta is cos inverse of two thirds, about forty eight degrees.

X2.text: Many students multiply matching parts, but keep the i, j and k. They write six i plus four k.

X3.text: But a dot product is a scalar. Add the parts into one number, ten. No i, no j, no k.

E1.text: Where is this asked? The angle between two vectors, checking for right angles, and work as F dot d.

Q1.text: Exam level now. A is four i, minus two j, plus four k. B is three j, plus four k. What is the component of A along B? Pause and solve.

A2.text: A dot B is zero, minus six, plus sixteen. That is ten.

A3.text: The size of B is the root of nine plus sixteen, which is five.

A4.text: The shadow of A on B is A dot B over B. Ten over five is two.

F1.text: Here is your recap. Screenshot this card.

Y1.text: Can you answer these three questions without help?

Y2.text: One. Why is the dot product a scalar, and not a vector?

Y3.text: Two. When is the dot product of two vectors zero?

Y4.text: Three. Why does a lower handle help Aarav pull his suitcase forward?

N1.text: Next time: carry a heavy bag across a room, and physics says you did no work on it. Really? We find out in work done by a constant force.
